description:
Dedicated Emmy Noether record for the Modern LaTeX Editions of Mathematics Manuscripts project. This record preserves source-checkable modern LaTeX working drafts, translations, source witnesses, render checks, and audit support for the Noether corpus.

Status at a glance. These files are working drafts and source-audit artifacts, not a certified critical edition. The current local TeX-changing German source-control candidate is R527; R528 and R529 are newer no-patch support layers for Paper 24 pp.250-261 and Papers 25-30 survival, not TeX heads and not reader releases. Older file-115/file-112 R124+P40 baseline packages remain preserved as source-repair/provenance layers, but they are not the current control summary. Treat the Noether record as a working source-control and multilingual translation lane, not Noether closure, whole-corpus certification, multilingual synchronization, or a critical edition.

Known caveat. Paper 40 uses the best staged local GDZ witness at native 400 ppi. That is below the preferred 650+ ppi threshold for final source certification and below the 1000+ ppi preference for dense mathematical material. The P40 repair should therefore be treated as best-available source repair work, not final high-resolution certification.

Survival audit cluster. File 114 Noether - R124plusP40 Survival NoNewPatch Audit Cluster 2026-06-24.zip aggregates Papers 09-20 survival/no-new-patch checks for the current R124+P40 baseline. It preserves audit evidence that prior source-critical repairs and known no-fix traps survive; it does not introduce a new canonical TeX body patch and is not whole-paper or whole-corpus certification.

Multilingual status. English, Spanish, Japanese, French, Chinese, Ukrainian, Russian, Interslavic, and other language branches are useful working translations, but remain downstream of the German/source audit line. The Slavic package is included as a work-so-far translation and linguistics lane, not source-certified closure.

GitHub mirror. Corrections, issue reports, and pull requests can be made through the public GitHub mirror.
